title: Static Equilibrium & Elasticity
summary: An object is in static equilibrium when both net force and net torque are zero. Solving requires choosing a pivot to eliminate unknowns. Materials deform under stress; within the elastic limit, strain is proportional to stress (Hooke's law for solids).

static equilibrium.plain: At rest with no net force and no net torque.

pivot choice.plain: Picking an axis to zero out an unknown force's torque.

center of gravity.in_class: Used to compute the weight's torque.

stress.plain: Force per unit area on a material.

elastic limit.in_class: Hooke's law holds only below it.

concept_sections.heading: Conditions for equilibrium
concept_sections.explanation: Two conditions must hold: the net force is zero (no translation) and the net torque is zero (no rotation). Both give equations to solve.
math_steps: Solve the system for the unknowns.

concept_sections.heading: Choosing a pivot
concept_sections.explanation: Torque depends on the chosen axis, so pick the pivot at an unknown force to eliminate its torque and simplify the equations.

concept_sections.heading: Center of gravity
concept_sections.explanation: An extended object's weight acts at its center of gravity. Use that point when computing the weight's torque.
math_steps: Include its torque about the pivot.

concept_sections.heading: Stress and strain
concept_sections.explanation: Stress is force per area, strain is fractional length change, and within the elastic limit they're proportional: $\sigma=Y\varepsilon$.

concept_sections.heading: Elasticity limits
concept_sections.explanation: Materials behave elastically (returning to shape) only up to the elastic limit; beyond it they deform permanently and eventually fracture.
math_steps: Stay below the elastic limit for Hooke's law.

real_world_examples.title: A ladder against a wall
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Force and torque balance (with friction at the base) keep it in equilibrium.

real_world_examples.title: A cantilever beam
real_world_examples.scenario: A balcony juts from a wall.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Torque balance about the wall determines the support forces.

real_world_examples.title: Stretching a steel cable
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Stress and Young's modulus predict the stretch $\Delta L$.

problems.prompt: A uniform $4$ m beam weighs $200$ N. Find the torque of its weight about one end.
problems.hint: Center of gravity at the middle.

problems.prompt: Two children balance a seesaw: $30$ kg at $2$ m. Find the torque about the pivot.

A $2$ m rod stretches $0.001$ m. Find the strain.
